name: Korg nanoKEY2

sources.title: nanoKEY2 Parameter Guide (KORG)
sources.note: factory settings: SUSTAIN button = CC 64, MOD button = CC 1 (momentary or toggle, on/off values editable); PITCH−/PITCH+ send pitch bend that returns to centre on release; keyboard, pitch, mod and sustain all transmit on the Global MIDI channel

sources.title: nanoKEY2 MIDI Implementation v1.00 (KORG)
sources.note: transmits note on/off (keyboard; note-off velocity 64), control change (MOD, SUSTAIN), pitch bend (PITCH buttons)

sources.title: nanoKEY2 Owner's Manual (KORG)
sources.note: ports: Mac "nanoKEY2 KEYBOARD" (in) / "nanoKEY2 CTRL" (out), Windows "nanoKEY2", with the KORG driver "nanoKEY2 1 KEYBOARD" / "nanoKEY2 1 CTRL"; OCT−/OCT+ shift ±4 octaves; 325 × 83 × 13 mm

notes: Factory settings. KORG does not print the factory Global MIDI channel; channel 1 is assumed (set it in KORG KONTROL Editor if yours differs, or use the element's channel attribute). PITCH− and PITCH+ are two buttons that send one pitch-bend message, so they are drawn as one bipolar strip. OCT−/OCT+ shift the keyboard inside the unit and send nothing of their own. No LED feedback.

controls.label: Keys
controls.note: Lowest key at octave 0 is not printed in the docs; 48 is assumed. Keys follow any note on the channel, so OCT−/OCT+ just scroll the on-screen keys.
